text:
maya: Quick check-in: ran a small bring-up of the new 30B-v2 quant (nf4 int4) with a scheduler that biases speculative picks by entropy-split. Results look...weird.
owen: what do you mean by "entropy-split" here? can you paste the scheduler policy?
maya: it's a tiny heuristic: if top-1 entropy < 0.8 -> allow speculative 2-step; else -> conservative single-step. code:
```
if entropy(top_k) < 0.8:
  speculative_budget = 2
else:
  speculative_budget = 1
```
maya: perf: ~1.9x p99 speedup on short chats (<=64 tokens). cost delta looks good. but qa metrics show a small regression on factuality tests (~1.7% drop on TruthBench subset).
nora: interesting. did you compare with unguided speculative baseline or with our usual uniform scheduler?
maya: compared to uniform-spec (we've used previously): uniform gives similar speed but larger quality drop (~3.5%). entropy-split is better but still a regression vs no-spec.
samir: any clues from log-level traces? maybe quantization + speculation interaction causing distribution shift in top-k?
maya: logs show more low-confidence rerolls - model often picks lower-likelihood tokens in step 1 and then the late-step overwrites, but earlier token choices change context. example snippet:
```
input: "When was the Eiffel Tower built?"
base top1: "1889"
spec step1 pick: "1887"
final: "1889"
```
maya: final is correct but internal trajectory seems off; downstream rerank metrics slightly worse.
own: can we run a tiny ablation: same scheduler on fp16 vs int4 quant on same model weights?
maya: queued that. initial fp16 run: regression disappears (TruthBench delta ~0.1%). so quantization is interacting badly with speculation.
ops-bot: [deploy] triggered job #4921 for scheduled ablation (fp16 vs int4) by maya
nora: let's also track by response length and presence of numeric tokens. hypothesis: quantization noise amplifies during speculative prefills for short numeric answers.
maya: agreed. next steps: 1) run fp16 vs int4 ablation (queued) 2) run variant where speculative picks are restricted to tokens in top-3 instead of free sample 3) add evaluation on number-focused subset and our default hallucination checks
samir: can I grab the logs?
maya: uploading in a minute to s3: s3://redwood-experiments/scheduler-entropy/1738809999/logs.tar.gz
nora: thanks. quick thought: maybe add a calibration pass where we score candidate speculative picks with a lightweight reranker before committing.
own: good idea. lightweight reranker could be 1-layer linear over logits -> cheap.
maya: ok will try reranker in next run. will post results here.
samir: :thumbsup:
maya: tagging @product for visibility (there's a small perf-quality tradeoff).
